source.text: Preserve the difference between the valid embedded deduction and the challenge to a proposed sufficient condition for knowledge.
source.locator: Printed pp. 121-122: initial assumptions and Case I

reading.speaker: Edmund L. Gettier
reading.summary: Preserve the difference between the valid embedded deduction and the challenge to a proposed sufficient condition for knowledge.

review.rationale: Imported design requirement; requires source-fidelity review. Mutation control: A reconstruction that makes justification factive changes the source assumptions and must be flagged.

premises: Separate actual-world truth from a subject's belief and justification.
Record the evidence and inference supporting a belief.
Track which object makes an existential description true.
Attribute the proposed knowledge analysis to the target view, not to Gettier's conclusion.
claim.conclusion: Never count a free assignment of Knowledge=false as discovery of a conceptual counterexample; knowledge attribution needs a declared interpretive judgment or reviewed case label.
